1.1 • What Is Nutrition?
11

BMI is a screening tool used to identify clients who are overweight or obese. Considering the recent policy 
change by the AMA, nurses should stay abreast of new research to determine how to incorporate BMI 
measurements when working with diverse client populations. BMI does not measure body fat directly but 
correlates with other more direct measures of body fat such as skinfold thickness measurements. High BMI can 
be correlated with obesity-linked adverse health outcomes. To determine BMI, input the client’s height and 
weight into the Adult BMI Calculator (https://openstax.org/r/cdchealthyweight). Use Table 1.2 to interpret the 
results.
